name: each party raises the other's public power to its own secret exponent
mechanism: each side picks a secret exponent and publishes the generator raised to it; each then raises the other's published value to its own secret; because exponents commute the two results agree, and an observer holding only the two published values cannot form it

sources.ref: List of algorithms (revid 1373672109), entry 'Diffie–Hellman key exchange' in section Computer science / Cryptography:

requires: a group where the exponent is hard to recover
an authenticated channel for the public values
fails_when: an active party in the middle substitutes both public values
